title: Replace a change of name certificate
summary: You can apply online to replace a change of name certificate if you registered the change since 1 April 1996.
intro:
If you've registered your own or your child's change of name since 1 April 1996 and you'd like a replacement change of name certificate, you can apply online.

If you changed your name by Deed Poll prior to the above date, call 13 77 88.
who_can_apply: You must have registered your own or your child's change of name since 1 April 1996.
If you are the person named on the certificate, or the parent of a child under 18, you can apply for a replacement.
If you are the parent of a child aged 18 or over, you are entitled to the replacement certificate if you applied for the original change of name.

If you are not the person named on the certificate or did not apply for the original change of name, you must meet specific criteria (e.g., providing a letter of authority, Power of Attorney, or being a solicitor).
If you changed your name by Deed Poll prior to 1 April 1996, you must call 13 77 88.
what_you_need: If applying for your certificate or your child's certificate, you need three forms of proof of identity.

If applying on behalf of someone else, you must provide a letter of authority giving permission to apply for a certificate (PDF), or show Power of Attorney relating to the person named on the certificate.
If you are a solicitor applying on behalf of a client, follow the specific information provided for solicitors.

how_to_steps.text: Ensure you meet the eligibility requirements.
Follow the prompts to apply for a replacement certificate.
Download and complete Replacement Change of Name Certificate Application – PDF.
Lodge it with the required documentation and payment using the details on the form.

more_info.text: If you begin filling in the online application form and want to save it to complete later, it's a simple step to resume your application
You're able to check the status of your application online.
Make sure that the copies of the documents you have scanned or photographed are clear and easy to read. The file types can be TIF, JPG or PDF (no spaces or dashes in the filename).

On successful receipt of your application form and payment you'll be sent a tax invoice to the email address you provided. You also have the option to print the summary page, or your entire application form.
Certificates are sent by the Registry of Births, Deaths & Marriages via registered post. They cannot be collected at a Service NSW Centre.
Processing times commence when applications are received in full compliance with Registry requirements, and exclude delivery time.

If you'd like your certificate to be sent to an Australian passport office, consulate or embassy, you'll need to make that request at the same time as your application, as this cannot be done later. Please include a request letter if mailing your application.
Make sure that you indicate which destination office you want the certificate sent to.
Certificates are not sent to foreign embassies, work email numbers or personal email numbers.
If you change your mind, or decide the certificate is no longer required, your application fee will not be refunded.
We suggest you do not laminate your certificates. Where possible, identity documents should be kept in their original state.

faqs.q: How do I replace a change of name certificate if I changed my name by Deed Poll before 1 April 1996?
faqs.a: If you changed your name by Deed Poll prior to 1 April 1996, you must call 13 77 88.

faqs.q: Who is eligible to apply for a replacement certificate?
faqs.a: You can apply if you are the person named on the certificate, or the parent of a child under 18. If you are the parent of a child aged 18 or over, you must have applied for the original change of name.

faqs.q: What do I need to apply for a replacement certificate?
faqs.a: If applying for your or your child's certificate, you need three forms of proof of identity. If applying on behalf of someone else, you need a letter of authority or Power of Attorney.
